title: Band with Lemon and the need for swing
summary: Playing with Lemon's band he told the leader to slow down and swing; recalls players such as Willie Paggio, Earl Wiggins and Thomas Jefferson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: While I was thinking I'd like to speak about that little band you had with Lemon at the...
Oh yeah, the band at the corner. Yeah, it is adorable. And it is adorable, yeah. Well we had Lemon and Johnny Green, you know Johnny Green. Wait a minute, is he the band of the bass player?
No, this was a white boy.

Yeah, he was a white boy playing with him. He lives over the river somewhere. He's a good musician. George used to call it New Orleans, he's a great band. He sells instruments. He sells guitars, he sells amplifiers, he sells... He's out in Indianapolis. He's any play, any reeds, he's got a system on the guitar that you can play any lead number you want in four frets. First four. First four frets, any first four frets that you want to play in.

You know you can't play race, you know racehorse music. That don't go. You're going too fast. Oh, pretty fast. Yeah. You know you've got to get a swing to your music, you know what I mean? And if you get a swing to your music people like music.
Who was singing it too fast?

Well Lemon was the ukulele player, he was our leader. Then he'd say it was grease your knuckles, grease your elbows. I said man you're playing the music too fast. I said people don't like that kind of music. I said give a swing to your music, you know what I mean? Bounce it a little bit. What you want about son?
He wants to see what the microphone is.
Go back one more. Go ahead son. Go ahead. See you after a while.
In the old days they usually play more slower.

We played, no, we played sort of swing music, you know what I mean? For a time music, you know what I mean? For people to dance. You know and if somebody would say well play us a fast number, we kind of play a little fast. But the majority of the music was a, you know sort of a nice beat. See that beat that Lewis has got? Same kind of beat. Lewis Armstrong. That kind of a beat. Full rhythm time, you see what I mean? If you're going to do it, you know, don't sound good. No. No, and there ain't got time to make it up. No, you got to give music a beat, you see what I mean? And I played a many jobs with Willie Paggio, you know him man. Sure. Well, and Earl, Earl Wiggins. Oh yeah, Earl Wiggins, yeah. Yeah, that's my piano player. And what's this guy named, Harold, Harold Dejon. Oh yeah. And you know who used to play with us? This boy was playing so much good cornet right now, he's going away I believe. He's a tall fella. Mike DeLay maybe? No, I've played with Mike DeLay, he's in California. He's tall. Yeah, but no this is a boy, they had a big write up in the paper about him about three or four months
ago. Jefferson, Thomas Jefferson. Thomas Jefferson. He's back again now.

Back again. Back again. Well they used to play with us. He didn't play to get paid, you know. He just played to set in with the band, you see what I mean? And oh man, you'd have so many musicians in there, I'm telling you the truth, I don't know where they'd all come from.
